title: Check account evidence without changing login policy
goal: Distinguish database consistency from authentication or access, using fabricated private group files and read-only evidence for an existing service identity.
challenge: Inspect the existing ll-service identity without changing it. Check the supplied private group/gshadow pairs, retain the rejected pair, repair a separate copy and prove consistency. Explain why neither a lock marker nor grpck success establishes all access behavior.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-accountfiles.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-accountfiles.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh identity.txt aging.txt rejected.txt good.group good.gshadow bad.group bad.gshadow originals.sha repaired.group repaired.gshadow && getent passwd ll-service > identity.txt && sudo passwd -S ll-service >> identity.txt && sudo chage -l ll-service > aging.txt && cat identity.txt aging.txt
steps.explanation: These are read-only inspections of an existing locked, non-login service account. Password locking, account expiry and shell restrictions have different scopes; do not edit them.
steps.expected: ll-service exists with a locked password and nologin shell. No policy changes.

steps.command: here && fresh good.group good.gshadow bad.group bad.gshadow originals.sha && printf 'll-note:x:49999:learner\n' > good.group && printf 'll-note:!::learner\n' > good.gshadow && cp -- good.group bad.group && cp -- good.gshadow bad.gshadow && cat good.group >> bad.group && sha256sum good.group good.gshadow bad.group bad.gshadow > originals.sha && timeout -k 1s 5s /usr/sbin/grpck -r good.group good.gshadow
steps.explanation: These are fabricated data files, not copies of real secrets or installed accounts. The alternate-file arguments and -r prevent database modification. A unique fake group name and matching member lists are checked against existing users.
steps.expected: Valid pair exits0; originals remain available.

steps.command: here && fresh rejected.txt && { timeout -k 1s 5s /usr/sbin/grpck -r bad.group bad.gshadow > rejected.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; test "$rc" = 2; } && sha256sum -c originals.sha && cat rejected.txt
steps.explanation: The duplicate is deliberately bad. Preserve status and diagnostic output; do not answer deletion prompts against live account databases.
steps.expected: Status2, duplicate finding, all source hashes unchanged.

steps.command: here && fresh repaired.group repaired.gshadow && awk -F: '!seen[$1]++' bad.group > repaired.group && cp -- good.gshadow repaired.gshadow && timeout -k 1s 5s /usr/sbin/grpck -r repaired.group repaired.gshadow && sha256sum -c originals.sha
steps.explanation: Repair a new copy, not either retained original. Consistency is not a login test or a grant of membership to the fictional group.
steps.expected: Separate repaired pair passes; no installed account or policy changed.

hints: Retain the bad pair and fix a new pair; a database check is not an access check.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 107.1 account databases; restricted-identity reinforcement. Self-reviewed and unscored; no complete-objective, exam-readiness or LPI-endorsement claim.
